description: The Jan21 report says “dozens,” and the Feb2 follow-up says “scores” for a Windhoek gathering dated Jan19; neither gives a numeric turnout. Workforce and interviewee counts are not protest attendance.
required_followup: Seek separate same-day estimates or organizer statements for Jan19 and Jan21; do not transfer the 1,980 unemployed-teacher pool or 200-plus Ohangwena interviewee figure to either gathering.

description: Neither the police-station release-demand gathering nor the later Yetu Complex crowd has a separate attendance count; injury counts are not attendance.
required_followup: Seek phase-specific NAMPA, NBC, police and Oshana/Oshakati regional reporting for a count at the station demand; do not infer that a later crowd count applies to the state-demand phase.

description: The state-directed police-station release demand followed an earlier arrest during a Shoprite sequence that began in December; its relation to the private wage campaign is unresolved, and later Yetu force is a separate reported phase.
required_followup: Compare December/January accounts and episode rules; keep private wage demands separate, distinguish the station demand from the later Yetu phase, and do not split only at the month boundary.

description: Accounts conflict over who initiated the later Yetu Complex confrontation and whether protesters threw stones; police rubber-bullet use is reported for that phase. Reporting does not establish that the later force responded to the earlier station release demand.
required_followup: Seek independent evidence about the Yetu Complex phase and keep its force facts scoped there; preserve uncertainty about whether that crowd was the same as the station release-demand crowd.

description: Informanté’s 16 January Oshakati article returned HTTP 429 and must not be retried; the NamibLII judgment PDF and Hitradio page produced tool errors, not site denials. Search snippets remain limited evidence.
required_followup: Try ordinary HTTPS access to the same public URLs and record actual status; do not bypass controls.

description: Searches include English, Afrikaans and a German Hitradio result. Q050–Q051 targeted Oshiwambo terms, but the returned relevant Omutumwa article is in English; no Oshiwambo-language source was established, and systematic Oshiwambo and other Namibian-language coverage remains incomplete.
required_followup: Search Oshiwambo and other relevant local-language sources with reviewed translations, plus regional outlets, and record actual source language and search outcomes.

description: Initial sources cover Windhoek, Oshakati, nationwide Shoprite reporting and a search-only Tsumeb branch closure result, but regional news and sector-by-sector coverage are incomplete.
required_followup: Search regional media and weekly/sector-specific reporting across all January weeks; open the Tsumeb result and resolve its local date/episode and count.

description: Namibian Lives Matter appears only in a radio snippet describing threatened court action over border killings; no January public gathering has been found.
required_followup: Search the movement and border-community terms in English, Afrikaans and local/regional reporting; a court threat alone is not a protest.

description: The Jan20 advance article says unemployed teachers also protested in 2020; the opened Sep10 report documents April/July 2020 petitions but no public gathering or date for that protest.
required_followup: Search contemporary 2020 coverage for the public protest referenced in the Jan20 advance report; petitions alone do not establish a gathering or continuity.

description: The current official baseline and additional Coding Procedure remain unresolved globally; the local May 2015 codebook is available.
required_followup: Coordinator to verify official baseline, current scope and episode rules before approval.

description: Opened 2 February reporting dates a Windhoek gathering to Jan19 and says a petition was delivered to the PM; Jan20 advance and Jan22 post-event reporting support an announced/reported Jan21 action. The Jan19 story may be a separate event or a date error; this is not resolved.
required_followup: Search Jan18–22 regional and local reporting, including the PM petition handover and organizer statements, for separate dates, locations and participation. Keep both candidate dates visible pending review; do not use the 200-plus Ohangwena interviewee figure as attendance.

description: A 26 January 2021 CIVICUS interview concerns #ShutItAllDown, but the linked opened feature describes a five-day protest wave in October 2020. No evidence found so far establishes a January 2021 continuation; publication date alone is insufficient.
required_followup: Keep the October wave outside the January unit and search for any January-dated public action before assigning continuity.

description: The 15 January Namibian Sun search result says Tsumeb community members joined Shoprite strikers and closed the branch on Tuesday morning; the 20 January Republikein issue search snippet says Shoprite workers protested the previous Wednesday. The weekday references imply adjacent dates if read literally, but may describe separate actions or phases. Neither result establishes exact local attendance.
required_followup: Open both articles if accessible and seek same-day Tsumeb reporting, union statements or local records to establish date, whether these were separate/continuing actions, local attendance and whether any state-directed demand existed.
